scenes.title: Cold open
narration: The Circle of the Amis
This is Amis harvest dance. Traditional.
on_screen: Title card: Amis harvest dance · Taiwan · Traditional

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: The harvest festival is held to celebrate the harvest of rice, which replaced millet as the primary crop.
It is a multi-day event lasting between one and seven days, depending on the specific tribe, and is held during the lunar months of July or August.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is part of the Ilisin festival, which serves to pray for agricultural success, population growth, and social cohesion.
It also functions as a space for partner selection and the evaluation of potential future leaders.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Participants dance hand-in-hand in a circle.
The primary movements are walking, running, and jumping.
The dance is led by a singer, and the movements vary by region, with coastal areas exhibiting more complex patterns.
Watch for Circular dance.
on_screen: Captions name each signature move as it appears
Formation: Circular formation with elders in the center.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is characterized by vocal chanting where a lead singer initiates the melody and the group responds, creating a serious and repetitive soundscape intended for communication with the spirit world.
on_screen: Instrument names on screen as each is mentioned

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Participants wear festival clothes, including hats decorated with rooster feathers.
The number of feathers on a hat symbolizes the wearer's status within the tribe.
on_screen: Image gallery: 1 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: The priest of the tribe is the primary figure in charge of the sacrificial rituals, instructing the community on farming activities and maintaining knowledge of the calendar, weather, and tribal history.
Dancing movements in coastal areas are more complicated and changeable than those in mountainous areas.
The dance belongs to the indigenous traditions of the Amis people in Taiwan, passed down through generations as part of the Ilisin festival.

scenes.title: A respectful note
narration: The songs and dances are considered a serious medium for communicating with ancestors and gods; outsiders should respect the solemnity of the rituals and the specific tribal protocols.
